nm2_1_modeling_methods.detail: Generalized Additive Models for Location, Scale and Shape (GAMLSS) with natural cubic spline functions (2 equally-spaced knots over age range 5-100 years) to model nonlinear age effects on both outcome mean (μ) and variance (σ). The model used generalized gamma distribution with natural logarithm linkage function for μ and σ, and identity linkage function for ν. Random intercepts for families were included to account for correlation between participants from the same families. Models were fitted separately for each hemisphere.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: Normative modeling of thalamic nuclei change over the lifespan was conducted using generalized additive models for location, scale, and shape (GAMLSS [57]); a robust and flexible framework for modeling nonlinear growth trajectories. GAMLSS models were fitted to thalamic nuclei volumes separately for each hemisphere to model nonlinear age effects (on the outcome mean and variance) over the lifespan

nm2_3_explanatory_variables.detail: Age modeled using natural cubic spline (ns) with 2 equally-spaced knots over age range 5-100 years, applied as nonlinear effect on both mean (μ) and variance (σ) parameters. Sex (male/female), Race (African American, Other, White), and estimated total intracranial volume (eTIV) included as fixed effects (β terms). Family-level random intercepts (α terms) included to account for correlation between participants from the same families in HCP Lifespan Cohort.
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.supporting_text: GAMLSS models were fitted to thalamic nuclei volumes separately for each hemisphere to model nonlinear age effects (on the outcome mean and variance) over the lifespan (ranging 5-100), stratified by sex, race, intracranial volumes and included random intercepts for families to account for the correlation between participants from the same families in the HCP Lifespan Cohort.
